title: A code explainer that is not allowed to invent
subtitle: Compute the call graph first, narrate second: putting deterministic evidence in front of the model

stats.label: of 294,362 code chunks covered by the graph

files, several languages, in the indexed monorepo

lede: Ask a language model how a piece of code works and it will tell you, fluently, including call paths that do not exist. Engineers act on those answers. I built a code-intelligence service where the model may only describe edges that a computed graph has already proven. The graph is extracted from source with a parser, dependency traces are plain database traversals with no model involved, and the explainer narrates only the evidence it is handed. If the graph's coverage is incomplete for a query, the answer is "coverage incomplete". A monorepo of around 19,000 files across several languages, used daily by AI agents that must understand blast radius before changing a symbol.
quote: A refusal beats a plausible guess, because the caveat is the first thing a reader stops seeing.
evidence: Code intelligence for AI agents: a tree-sitter call graph over a 19,000-file multi-language monorepo, with 294,033 of 294,362 code chunks covered.
Hallucination prevention by design: the model narrates only a path the graph has proven, and a query the graph cannot fully cover returns coverage incomplete instead of a guess.
Graph queries in SQL: dependency tracing as a bounded breadth-first search over partitioned edge tables, with 0 model calls in a trace.
Index lifecycle design: edges move from pending to active as their endpoints are indexed, and graph generations let the index rebuild without serving a half-built graph.
author: Corey James
